Hi Sam

Thanks again for the call earlier  really helpful to understand Acme's integration goals. Quick recap + open items so we can keep momentum: 

Summary from our side:
- Goal: Embed Redwood inference into Acme's content platform for assisted writing + semantic search/QA.
- Priority integration paths: 1) In-app generative suggestions (structured output / tool calling), 2) semantic search + reranking for results, 3) streaming responses for live UX.

Action items / open questions (please confirm or add):
1) SDK & Auth: you preferred short-lived tokens via your internal auth system. Are you planning to mint per-user API keys (server-side) or want Redwood to support delegated OAuth flows? (We support both.)
2) Routing: will requests be pinned to a single region (US-east) or do you need multi-region routing for latency?
3) Request/response schema: for structured output + tool-calling we recommended the chat-style API (structured JSON) over legacy completions. Any constraints on field names or validation schema on your side?
4) Tokenization / max_tokens: what max response length do you expect in characters or tokens? We can propose a default (response <= 512 tokens) but need to know your UI truncation limits.
5) Streaming semantics & stop behavior: do you need partial JSON streaming (object-per-event) or SSE-style delta tokens? This impacts how we recommend stop sequences and framing.
6) Embeddings vs reranker: is your pipeline: (a) semantic search -> top-K -> rerank with model scoring, or (b) rerank-only downstream?

Attachments: redwood-integration-guide.pdf  quick SDK snippets and streaming examples.

Proposed next step: Tech deep-dive with Ethan (SE) and Lauren (solutions) to go over schema + a sample request/response contract. Are you available Thu 4/22 10am PT?

Thanks

Thanks Sam  appreciate the details and the sample. Adding technical notes below to address streaming, tokenization, and schema recommendations.

Short answers up front:
- Use chat-style API for structured output/tool-calling. It provides clearer intent (role/message) and better streaming semantics for JSON/tool calls.
- For partial JSON streaming we recommend event-delimited objects (SSE or JSON-lines) rather than trying to stream a single JSON document character-by-character it's more robust for clients.
- Token counting: follow our chat tokenization guide  we count per-message overhead (role/name tokens) + content tokens. We can provide a small utility in the SDK to precompute token usage.

Details / recommendations:
1) Chat vs Completions: 
- Chat API (recommended): messages = [{role:system},{role:user},{role:assistant}] with support for structured tool-calls (name + arguments). For structured output, include an explicit tools schema and encourage the assistant to return JSON payloads in a dedicated field (e.g., "tool_result").
- Completions: still supported but less ergonomic for multi-turn or tool-calling. Use only for single-turn generation without structured fields.

2) Structured output + streaming semantics:
- Pattern A (recommended): Stream incremental "events" where each event is a small JSON object representing a partial field or delta, e.g.:
  {"event":"field","name":"title","value":"Draft title..."}
  {"event":"field","name":"summary","value":"First sentence..."}
  {"event":"done"}
- Pattern B (alternative): Stream plain tokens and have client reconstruct full JSON - riskier because of partial parse failures.

3) Stop tokens / framing:
- If using event-delimited JSON, set stop sequences to a single delimiter (e.g., "\n\nEND_EVENT\n\n") and emit explicit "done" event. This avoids ambiguous JSON truncation.
- Avoid relying on punctuation-only stops when streaming structured output.

4) Tokenization and max_tokens guidance:
- Token accounting includes: system message tokens, user/assistant role tokens, and the content tokens. For chat we add ~4 tokens of overhead per message (varies by model).
- Practical rule: compute available model context (model_max_tokens) - estimated prompt_tokens - reserve (safety_margin). For UI-friendly outputs we usually reserve 128-256 tokens for safety. Example: for a 4096-context model and a 1024-token prompt, set max_tokens <= 4096-1024-256 = 2816.
- For structured JSON responses, keep output <= 512 tokens for predictable rendering and latency; if you need longer fields, stream them as events in chunks.

5) Embeddings + Reranker:
- Use embeddings to do candidate retrieval (semantic search) across your corpus (Top-K ~ 50).
- Use the reranker (model scoring) to rescore the Top-K with context-aware prompts. Reranker can be cheaper if run on a smaller model with a tight prompt focusing on ranking.
- We recommend caching embeddings for static documents and using incremental reindexing for content changes.

6) SDK & Auth notes:
- SDK supports API-key header authorization and a rotating short-lived key flow. We can add client helpers to fetch rotated keys from your auth service.
- For server-to-server calls pin endpoint to US-East for now; later we can add route policies if you need multi-region.

Sample request (high-level):
POST /v1/chat/complete
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <REDWOOD_KEY>
Body: {
  "model":"redwood-chat-1",
  "messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a JSON-output assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Generate fields: title, summary"}],
  "stream":true,
  "stop":["\n\nEND_EVENT\n\n"],
  "max_tokens":512
}
